title: Matrix Multiplication Tensor Rank
tagline: Strassen multiplied 2x2 with 7 mults in 1969. For 5x5, the record is 96. Beat it.
description: Find a way to multiply matrices using fewer scalar multiplications than the current record. For example, the naive way to multiply two 3x3 matrices uses 27 multiplications, but it can be done in 23. For 5x5, naive uses 125 but the record is 96. Both square (n x n) and rectangular (n x m times m x p) cases count.
context: Strassen (1969) showed 2x2 can be done in 7 instead of 8, the first proof that matrix multiplication is sub-cubic. For 3x3, the record of 23 has stood since 1976 (lower bound: 19). DeepMind's AlphaTensor (2022) found improvements over finite fields but matched or fell short over the integers for these sizes. Rectangular cases like R(2,3,4) and R(3,3,6) are less studied and may be more tractable. All submissions must work over standard arithmetic (integers/rationals).

leaderboard.note: Records over integers/rationals. Finite-field results (e.g. AlphaTensor over F2) excluded.

rows.note: Lower bound 49 - tight but optimality unproved

verification: Runs the algorithm on 100 random integer matrix pairs (n x m times m x p). Checks exact equality with the true product A*B. All coefficients must be rational.

suggestedApproach.title: Implement Strassen
suggestedApproach.body: The 2x2 case with 7 multiplications. Understand how 7 products reconstruct all 4 output entries - this is the template for all tensor-rank algorithms.

suggestedApproach.title: Pick a target
suggestedApproach.body: R(5,5,5) has the largest gap for square cases. Rectangular cases like R(3,3,6) and R(4,4,5) are less studied and may yield to fresh approaches.

suggestedApproach.title: Tensor decomposition
suggestedApproach.body: The multiplication tensor for (n,m,p) has shape nm x mp x np. Decompose it into r rank-1 terms. Each term = one scalar multiplication in the algorithm.

suggestedApproach.title: Search methods
suggestedApproach.body: Gradient descent on decomposition error with random restarts. AlphaTensor used MCTS + RL. Simpler evolutionary approaches also work.

agentPrompt: I want you to find a bilinear algorithm for multiplying two 3x3x6 matrices (a 3x3 matrix times a 3x6 matrix) using fewer than 40 scalar multiplications over the integers. Represent the algorithm as a tensor decomposition: three lists U, V, W of length r (the number of multiplications). For each t in 1..r: U[t] is a 3x3 matrix of coefficients applied to A, V[t] is a 3x6 matrix applied to B, and W[t] is a 3x6 matrix of reconstruction weights. The product is C = sum_t W[t] * (sum(U[t] * A) * sum(V[t] * B)). Verify by testing on random integer matrices. Output U, V, W as JSON arrays.

bounds.name: Best 23, lower bound 19
bounds.formula: Makarov & Laderman (1976). Gap open for 50 years.

bounds.name: Less studied
bounds.formula: Lower bounds weaker. R(2,3,4), R(3,3,6), R(4,4,5) all have room.

bounds.name: Exponent <= 2.371552
bounds.formula: Williams et al. (2024). Lower bound 2. Whether omega = 2 is open.
